resources.title: AI model
resources.note: The trained "brain" that produces answers. ChatGPT and Claude are apps built on AI models.

extra.definition: The trained "brain" that produces answers. ChatGPT and Claude are apps built on AI models.

resources.title: LLM
resources.note: Large language model: an AI model trained on huge amounts of text so it can read and write.

extra.definition: Large language model: an AI model trained on huge amounts of text so it can read and write.

resources.title: Prompt
resources.note: The message or instructions you type to an AI.

extra.definition: The message or instructions you type to an AI.

resources.title: Token
resources.note: A small chunk of text (roughly ¾ of a word). AI reads, writes and charges by tokens.

extra.definition: A small chunk of text (roughly ¾ of a word). AI reads, writes and charges by tokens.

resources.title: Context window
resources.note: How much text an AI can look at in one go, like its short-term working memory.

extra.definition: How much text an AI can look at in one go, like its short-term working memory.

resources.title: Hallucination
resources.note: When an AI states something false with confidence. Always check important facts.

extra.definition: When an AI states something false with confidence. Always check important facts.

resources.title: Agent
resources.note: An AI that can use tools and take steps on its own to finish a task.

extra.definition: An AI that can use tools and take steps on its own to finish a task.

resources.title: RAG
resources.note: Retrieval-augmented generation: the AI looks up your documents before answering.

extra.definition: Retrieval-augmented generation: the AI looks up your documents before answering.

resources.title: Embedding
resources.note: A list of numbers that captures the meaning of a piece of text, so computers can compare meanings.

extra.definition: A list of numbers that captures the meaning of a piece of text, so computers can compare meanings.

resources.title: Vector database
resources.note: A database built to store embeddings and find similar meanings quickly.

extra.definition: A database built to store embeddings and find similar meanings quickly.

resources.title: MCP
resources.note: Model Context Protocol: a standard way to connect AI assistants to apps and data.

extra.definition: Model Context Protocol: a standard way to connect AI assistants to apps and data.

resources.title: A2A
resources.note: Agent2Agent: a standard way for AI agents from different companies to work together.

extra.definition: Agent2Agent: a standard way for AI agents from different companies to work together.

resources.title: Fine-tuning
resources.note: Extra training on your own examples to specialise an existing model.

extra.definition: Extra training on your own examples to specialise an existing model.

resources.title: Open-source
resources.note: Software whose code is public and free to use, change and share.

extra.definition: Software whose code is public and free to use, change and share.

resources.title: API
resources.note: A way for one program to talk to another. Developers use APIs to add AI to their apps.

extra.definition: A way for one program to talk to another. Developers use APIs to add AI to their apps.

resources.title: GPU
resources.note: A powerful chip that does the heavy maths needed to train and run AI models.

extra.definition: A powerful chip that does the heavy maths needed to train and run AI models.

resources.title: Eval
resources.note: A test that checks how well an AI performs on a set of example questions.

extra.definition: A test that checks how well an AI performs on a set of example questions.

resources.title: Open-weight model
resources.note: An AI model you can download and run yourself, such as Llama or Gemma.

extra.definition: An AI model you can download and run yourself, such as Llama or Gemma.

resources.title: Machine learning
resources.note: Teaching computers to make predictions by learning from examples instead of fixed rules.

extra.definition: Teaching computers to make predictions by learning from examples instead of fixed rules.

resources.title: Neural network
resources.note: Layers of simple maths units that together learn patterns, loosely inspired by the brain.

extra.definition: Layers of simple maths units that together learn patterns, loosely inspired by the brain.

resources.title: Training data
resources.note: The examples a model learns from. Its quality decides how good the model is.

extra.definition: The examples a model learns from. Its quality decides how good the model is.

resources.title: Bias
resources.note: When an AI treats some people or cases unfairly, usually because of skewed training data.

extra.definition: When an AI treats some people or cases unfairly, usually because of skewed training data.

resources.title: Prompt injection
resources.note: Hidden instructions in a web page or file that trick an AI into doing something it shouldn't.

extra.definition: Hidden instructions in a web page or file that trick an AI into doing something it shouldn't.

resources.title: Diffusion model
resources.note: The kind of AI behind most image and video generators. It turns random noise into a picture step by step.

extra.definition: The kind of AI behind most image and video generators. It turns random noise into a picture step by step.

resources.title: Computer vision
resources.note: AI that understands images and video.

extra.definition: AI that understands images and video.

resources.title: Multimodal
resources.note: An AI that works with more than one kind of input, like text plus images or audio.

extra.definition: An AI that works with more than one kind of input, like text plus images or audio.

resources.title: Temperature
resources.note: A setting that controls how creative or predictable an AI's answers are. Low = safe and consistent, high = more varied.

extra.definition: A setting that controls how creative or predictable an AI's answers are. Low = safe and consistent, high = more varied.

resources.title: Inference
resources.note: Using a trained AI model to get an answer. Every time you send a prompt, the model runs inference.

extra.definition: Using a trained AI model to get an answer. Every time you send a prompt, the model runs inference.

resources.title: Parameters
resources.note: The millions or billions of numbers inside a model that it learned during training. More parameters usually means a bigger, more capable model.

extra.definition: The millions or billions of numbers inside a model that it learned during training. More parameters usually means a bigger, more capable model.

resources.title: Reasoning model
resources.note: An AI model that "thinks" step by step before answering, which helps with maths, code and planning but takes longer.

extra.definition: An AI model that "thinks" step by step before answering, which helps with maths, code and planning but takes longer.

resources.title: Transformer
resources.note: The design behind almost all modern language models. It lets the model look at every word in a sentence at once to understand context.

extra.definition: The design behind almost all modern language models. It lets the model look at every word in a sentence at once to understand context.

resources.title: System prompt
resources.note: Hidden instructions given to an AI before your message, setting its role, tone and rules.

extra.definition: Hidden instructions given to an AI before your message, setting its role, tone and rules.

resources.title: Few-shot prompting
resources.note: Showing the AI a few examples of what you want inside your prompt so it copies the pattern.

extra.definition: Showing the AI a few examples of what you want inside your prompt so it copies the pattern.

resources.title: Guardrails
resources.note: Rules and checks around an AI app that block unsafe, off-topic or wrong outputs.

extra.definition: Rules and checks around an AI app that block unsafe, off-topic or wrong outputs.

resources.title: Benchmark
resources.note: A standard test used to compare AI models, like an exam everyone takes.

extra.definition: A standard test used to compare AI models, like an exam everyone takes.

resources.title: Overfitting
resources.note: When a model memorises its training examples instead of learning general patterns, so it does badly on new data.

extra.definition: When a model memorises its training examples instead of learning general patterns, so it does badly on new data.

resources.title: Quantization
resources.note: Shrinking a model by storing its numbers with less precision, so it runs faster on smaller computers with a small quality loss.

extra.definition: Shrinking a model by storing its numbers with less precision, so it runs faster on smaller computers with a small quality loss.

resources.title: Distillation
resources.note: Training a small, cheap model to copy the answers of a big model.

extra.definition: Training a small, cheap model to copy the answers of a big model.

resources.title: Grounding
resources.note: Making an AI base its answer on specific trusted sources (like your documents) instead of only its memory.

extra.definition: Making an AI base its answer on specific trusted sources (like your documents) instead of only its memory.

resources.title: Knowledge cutoff
resources.note: The date after which a model has no training data, so it doesn't know about later events unless given search or documents.

extra.definition: The date after which a model has no training data, so it doesn't know about later events unless given search or documents.

resources.title: Human in the loop
resources.note: A setup where a person reviews or approves the AI's work before it takes effect.

extra.definition: A setup where a person reviews or approves the AI's work before it takes effect.

resources.title: Deepfake
resources.note: A fake image, video or voice made with AI to look or sound like a real person.

extra.definition: A fake image, video or voice made with AI to look or sound like a real person.

resources.title: Synthetic data
resources.note: Artificial data created by computers or AI, used to train or test models when real data is scarce or private.

extra.definition: Artificial data created by computers or AI, used to train or test models when real data is scarce or private.

resources.title: AGI
resources.note: Artificial general intelligence: a hypothetical AI that can learn and do almost any intellectual task a person can.

extra.definition: Artificial general intelligence: a hypothetical AI that can learn and do almost any intellectual task a person can.
